styles.name: Paper Cutout
styles.description: A mascot made from clean scissor-cut paper shapes with a single visible material layer.

instructions.materials: Use opaque matte colored paper with a slight paper thickness visible at selected cut edges.
instructions.forms: Construct broad rounded paper shapes with simple joined limbs and generous facial spacing.
instructions.linework: Define contours through clean scissor-cut borders and use a few dark paper pieces for features.
instructions.shading: Keep fills nearly flat with minimal edge thickness shading and no cast shadow outside the figure.
instructions.palette: Choose a small set of solid paper colors with strong separation between face and body shapes.
instructions.texture: Suggest a fine paper tooth inside large fills while keeping cut borders smooth and deliberate.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated flat paper mascot with consistent cut shapes and no supporting sheet or tabletop.

negative_constraints: Do not add deep stacked layers or fold the character into origami.
Avoid scissors, glue marks, isolated confetti, and paper backgrounds.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Clean craft mascots, educational cutouts, and simple animation poses.
limitations: A flat construction needs silhouette-led poses; foreshortening should not invent new paper layers.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Use antialiased paper borders and keep any white paper pieces opaque during keying.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Layered Paper
styles.description: A shallow paper relief whose stepped layers construct the character volume without an surrounding scene.

instructions.materials: Use stacked matte paper sheets with visible thickness and a few nested cut shapes per body part.
instructions.forms: Build shallow relief volumes from broad inset layers, keeping limbs attached and the outer contour simple.
instructions.linework: Let crisp stacked sheet boundaries define facial planes and markings without a drawn outline.
instructions.shading: Use narrow contact shadows only between layers, with consistent shallow depth and fixed light direction.
instructions.palette: Choose related paper shades for depth and one clear accent color for identity-critical markings.
instructions.texture: Keep surfaces mostly smooth with restrained paper fibers; emphasize the stepped edge structure.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated layered paper character in a consistent shallow view with no shadow-box background.

negative_constraints: Do not generate a scenic layered-paper landscape or enclosing frame.
Avoid dozens of thin layers, dramatic cast shadows, and detached paper clouds.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Dimensional craft mascots and character relief illustrations.
limitations: Layer count should stay low so relief depth remains readable at sprite size.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Retain alpha outside the outer layer; interior contact shadows must remain part of the opaque artwork.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Papercraft
styles.description: A three-dimensional folded-and-glued paper model with broad planar facets and visible assembly seams.

instructions.materials: Use thick printed paper or cardstock folded and glued into a simple hollow model.
instructions.forms: Construct the head and body from broad planar facets with compact folded limbs and a stable low-detail silhouette.
instructions.linework: Show a few fold creases and edge joins; print facial features cleanly onto large front-facing planes.
instructions.shading: Shade planar faces in discrete values and use only shallow seam occlusion at folds.
instructions.palette: Use solid printed color regions with a few darker facet tones and stable marking placement.
instructions.texture: Suggest smooth cardstock and subtle crease wear without photographic paper wrinkles.
instructions.rendering: Render an assembled paper model with consistent fold topology and no unfolded template beside it.

negative_constraints: Do not show glue tabs, cutting diagrams, or flat assembly nets.
Avoid excessive triangulation, fragile paper spikes, and large floor shadows.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Craft-model mascots and low-detail dimensional character assets.
limitations: The image is an illustration of a paper model, not a validated fabrication net.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Use antialiased facet edges and preserve opaque pale paper; key colors must be absent from printed faces.

styles.name: Origami
styles.description: A mascot expressed through a restrained single-sheet folding language with clean creases and large readable planes.

instructions.materials: Use one or two coordinated sheets of matte folding paper with a visible contrasting reverse when folded.
instructions.forms: Express anatomy through a few purposeful folds, broad planar heads, and short triangular or folded limbs.
instructions.linework: Use crease lines and folded borders sparingly; keep facial details as minimal approved surface marks.
instructions.shading: Shade adjoining planes with simple value steps and tight crease shadows without broad environmental lighting.
instructions.palette: Preserve the chosen paper face and reverse colors across all folds and animation states.
instructions.texture: Keep the paper surface smooth with subtle crease compression and no cloth or clay grain.
instructions.rendering: Render a plausible folded-paper character with consistent major folds and a compact self-supporting silhouette.

negative_constraints: Do not add cut-and-glued fragments that contradict the folded-sheet appearance.
Avoid needle-thin folded points, unfolding diagrams, and disconnected paper pieces.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Elegant geometric pets and paper-folding-inspired mascots.
limitations: Animated poses are stylized illustrations rather than mechanically proven origami fold sequences.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Preserve antialiased fold tips without smoothing away creases; inspect pale reverse-paper regions during keying.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Paper Quilling
styles.description: A mascot built from broad rolled paper coils and upright curved paper strips.

instructions.materials: Use narrow but visibly thick colored paper strips rolled into open coils and curved upright borders.
instructions.forms: Construct large body regions from a few nested coils contained by an attached outer paper contour.
instructions.linework: Use upright strip edges as deliberate curved linework and broader filled shapes for eyes and mouth.
instructions.shading: Apply shallow relief shading inside coils and narrow strip-contact shadows with one stable light direction.
instructions.palette: Choose a coordinated strip palette with strong contrast between outer contour, inner coils, and facial features.
instructions.texture: Show smooth paper edges and broad concentric winding; avoid tiny densely packed spirals.
instructions.rendering: Render a quilled character on transparency with opaque core regions behind the face and major limbs.

negative_constraints: Do not add a card backing or decorative swirls outside the character.
Avoid hair-thin strips, countless tiny coils, and transparent facial features.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Decorative paper mascots and rounded craft emblems.
limitations: Open coils need sufficiently broad strips; dense quilling can become unreadable at small size.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Prefer alpha for intentional coil apertures; visual review must distinguish designed holes from extraction damage.

styles.name: Torn-Paper Collage
styles.description: A character assembled from broad torn paper shapes with controlled fibrous borders.

instructions.materials: Use matte colored paper torn into broad shapes, showing occasional lighter paper fibers along tears.
instructions.forms: Build a bold character silhouette from overlapping irregular pieces with larger uncomplicated face shapes.
instructions.linework: Let the torn contours define anatomy and use a few deliberate dark paper fragments for the face.
instructions.shading: Keep color pieces mostly flat with subtle overlap depth and no independent floor shadow.
instructions.palette: Use a limited collage palette with clear contrasts and stable individual paper-piece colors.
instructions.texture: Show uneven torn edges and restrained paper grain, concentrating roughness away from the eyes.
instructions.rendering: Render attached torn-paper components with fixed piece placement and no scattered scraps outside the figure.

negative_constraints: Do not smooth every tear into machine-cut vector curves.

styles.name: Mixed-Media Collage
styles.description: A coordinated mascot combining a few visibly different paper, paint, and pencil techniques.

instructions.materials: Combine cut paper body pieces, opaque painted markings, and a few colored-pencil feature lines.
instructions.forms: Use broad collage shapes to establish anatomy and reserve material changes for clearly defined character regions.
instructions.linework: Pair cut-paper contours with deliberate pencil or ink facial lines, keeping each tool role consistent.
instructions.shading: Use flat paper planes with selective painted shading rather than unrelated lighting effects on each piece.
instructions.palette: Unify the different media through a small repeated palette and one stable high-contrast facial treatment.
instructions.texture: Show paper tooth, restrained brush marks, and sparse pencil grain in separate readable areas.
instructions.rendering: Render one coherent isolated character, retaining the approved medium assignment for every body part across frames.

negative_constraints: Do not turn the image into a mood board with photos, captions, or background scraps.
Avoid arbitrary medium switching and texture overload on the face.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Expressive art-room mascots and distinctive editorial characters.
limitations: Use at most a few complementary media so the identity remains stable and visually coherent.

styles.name: Scrapbook

instructions.materials: Use patterned scrapbook paper, matte cardstock, and one or two attached paper tabs or stitched embellishments.
instructions.forms: Construct the character from broad layered paper shapes with simple rounded limbs and a clear central face.
instructions.linework: Use clean cut edges, occasional dashed faux-stitch borders, and bold paper facial marks.
instructions.shading: Apply shallow layer-overlap shadows while keeping printed patterns flat and subordinate to character volume.
instructions.palette: Coordinate two or three paper colors and one restrained repeated pattern with strong facial contrast.
instructions.texture: Show a few visible printed motifs and subtle paper tooth, keeping pattern registration stable.
instructions.rendering: Render a character-shaped scrapbook assembly without a page, journal, photograph, or surrounding decorative layout.

negative_constraints: Do not generate captions, dates, readable labels, or scrapbook pages.
Avoid detached stickers, tiny embellishments, and patterns that compete with the face.
